topic_title: The Coup Anniversary Chile's Government Skipped

slides.headline: For the First Time, Chile Said Nothing
slides.body: In 2026, Chile's government held no official ceremony for the 1973 coup — the first silence since democracy returned in 1990.

slides.headline: September 11, 1973: Pinochet's Coup
slides.body: General Augusto Pinochet overthrew elected president Salvador Allende, who died defending La Moneda palace, launching 17 years of dictatorship.

slides.headline: President José Antonio Kast Chose Silence
slides.body: Kast, an open Pinochet admirer, skipped the ceremony and left Santiago — the first president since 1990 to do so.

slides.headline: 2,279 Political Killings, One Silent State
slides.body: Chile's Rettig Commission documented 2,279 political killings and 957 forced disappearances under Pinochet — victims this year's government did not name.

slides.headline: Families Still Wait for Answers
slides.body: Hundreds of the disappeared were never found. Former presidents Boric and Bachelet marked the day; Kast's government did not.

slides.headline: Can a Nation Forget on Purpose?
slides.body: Chile's government called the silence a bid for unity. Fifty-three years later, who gets to decide what a country remembers?
